title: ops-pocket-weekly-prep-owen
body:
Context:
- Quick personal prep for the weekly serving-runtime / infra / console bridge sync. Meant to be a compact pocket agenda I can paste in Slack as the meeting opener. Keep it under 20 minutes for the triage section, then 30m for deeper topics if needed.

Goals for this meeting:
- Surface any latency regressions since the last deploy and decide immediate mitigations.
- Confirm rollout status for kernel-selection change on canary (region-us-west-2).
- Capture follow-ups clearly (owner + due date) so I can push them into the sprint board.

Top-level metrics (quick snapshot I will copy from dashboards before the call):
- 95p latency (inference): ~42ms (baseline target 35ms) — note +7ms spike last 48h in us-west-2.
- Error rate (model-serving): 0.6% (target <0.25%) — bulk of errors are transient K/V cache misses reported by service X.
- QPS (hosted tier): 2.4k avg, burst peak 3.1k — autoscaler held up but saturation signs on small instances.

Agenda (starter):
1) 5m - Quick round-robin: blockers or fires? (keep to 30s per person)
2) 10m - Latency blip: observations + immediate mitigation proposals
   - Aisha: heap/kv cache stats from recent patch
   - Diego: kernel-selection rollout telemetry from canary
3) 10m - Canary rollout status and rollback criteria (serve-runtime#918 notes)
4) 10m - Console UX: tracing links broken when requests proxy to dedicated clusters (UX impact)
5) 5m - Action items + owners + due dates (capture final)

Talking points / prompts I want to say:
- "If the 95p stays >40ms after 2 hours with no config changes, prefer temporary routing to smaller model variant for latency SLO adherence."
- "Let's not conflate cache miss errors with model quality; treat as infra incident until proven otherwise."
- "If autoscaler shows sustained CPU >75% on small nodes for 30+ mins, we should flip burst-policy to add ephemeral machines — Diego, can you confirm ETA?"

Open questions I want answered in-meeting:
- Is the kernel-selection change (PR linked) actually increasing memory churn on smaller instance types? (need raw heap/delta metrics)
- Any evidence the KV cache TTL bump last week correlates to miss storms when traffic patterns shift?
- Are any customer routes impacted or only internal test routes? list of route ids?

Immediate proposed mitigations (to discuss):
- Short-term: Canary rollback to previous kernel for us-west-2 if 95p >45ms over next 2 hours. (owner: Owen)
- Mid-term: Enable prefix-only caching for top 10 routes to reduce KV lookups (owner: Aisha)
- Longer-term: Add memory churn metric to canary gating and alerting (owner: Diego)

Action items (draft — will confirm owners in meeting):
- AI-1: Collect per-instance heap and GC pause metrics for canary hosts (Jenkins job + dashboard panel). owner: Aisha; due: 2026-03-13
- AI-2: If 95p remains >45ms after 2 hours, trigger rollback and route traffic to model-v1b variant. owner: Owen; due: 2026-03-12 16:30 (local follow-up window)
- AI-3: Patch autoscaler policy to allow one additional ephemeral small node on sustained CPU >75% for 20m. owner: Diego; due: 2026-03-16
- AI-4: Console team to fix tracing link resolution when proxied to dedicated clusters (bug ticket created). owner: Mikael; due: 2026-03-19
- AI-5: Add a regression test case to CI that simulates KV cache TTL shifts and measures miss-rate ripple. owner: Eng-qa (assign: Priya); due: 2026-03-20

Notes-to-self / prep checklist before the call:
- Pull latest 95/99 latency charts for us-west-2 and attach to the meeting thread.
- Open PR #918 and flag the exact commits that could cause memory churn.
- DM Diego to have his canary host ids ready (so we can jump into instance-level metrics quickly).
- Draft Slack opener with TL;DR and the three asks: (1) quick blockers callout, (2) consent to rollback criteria, (3) confirm owners.

Risky assumptions I'm testing in this sync:
- That the latency increase is infra-related, not model size/sequence-length shift.
- That rollback to the previous kernel will reduce latency without reintroducing other errors.

Follow-up formatting I will use after meeting (paste to sprint board):
- [AI-#] short title | owner | due | status | linked tickets/PRs

Personal closing note (for my journal):
- If we roll back, plan a postmortem step to measure if cache miss patterns change — want concrete acceptance criteria for 'safe to re-roll forward'.
- Keep this doc as the single source for the quick meeting opener; archive the final action-items into the sprint board and set reminders.

Quick copy snippet for Slack opener (short):
"Ops pocket sync: quick 20m triage on us-west-2 latency spike + canary kernel rollout. Bring canary host ids and heap metrics. Goal = decide mitigation (rollback vs config tweak) and assign owners. See notes in pinned doc."

-- end of scratchpad --
summary: Pocket agenda + action tracker for weekly serving-runtime / infra / console bridge. Focus: latency spike in us-west-2, canary kernel rollout, console tracing links. Contains metrics snapshot placeholders, proposed mitigations, open questions, and 5 draft action items with owners and due dates.
